title: Lior and the Trail
premise: Railroad engineer Mara Lockridge inherits a dying prospector's map to the Silverthread headwaters, land sealed by a mining concession that expires in thirty days. Racing upstream with her estranged brother Eli, whose railroad company secretly bankrolled the concession, she must choose between exposing the fraud that would save her career and protecting the river town that took her in. When the permits expire and the company's enforcers arrive, Mara burns her own survey of the line, testifying that the route is unbuildable — trading her profession for the truth. The town holds; the river stays wild; and Mara, no longer an engineer of rails but a keeper of maps, finally belongs somewhere she cannot own.
about_author: Sable Halloran is a former backcountry surveyor who spent six seasons mapping watersheds across the northern ranges before turning to fiction. She writes adventure novels about people who measure the world and discover it measures them back.

chapters.title: The Weight of Iron
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Surveying a doomed mountain spur, she clashes with company men who want the numbers fudged. Establishes her precision, her pride in the railroad, and her loneliness after years on the road. Emotional beat: competence as armor.

chapters.title: A Stranger's Bargain
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. A prospector named Amos Craw dies in her survey camp, trading a hand-drawn map of the Silverthread headwaters for a promise: take it to the town of Kestrel Falls before the snows. Emotional beat: a debt incurred against her will.

chapters.title: Kestrel Falls
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. She arrives in the river town expecting to hand off the map and leave, but finds the townsfolk wary, grieving men lost to the closed mines, and a sheriff who recognizes Amos's name. Emotional beat: unwanted belonging.

chapters.title: The Brother at the Depot
chapters.summary: Eli's POV. Eli Lockridge arrives representing the railroad's new concession partner, stunned to find his sister entangled with the very valley his company intends to strip. He hides the partnership's true terms from her. Emotional beat: love curdling into secrecy.

chapters.title: What the Map Shows
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Studying Amos's map beside her own surveys, she realizes the concession's claimed ore body sits inside the river's source — meaning the mine would poison Kestrel Falls' water. Emotional beat: knowledge as burden.

chapters.title: Thirty Days
chapters.summary: Sheriff Ada Voss's POV. Ada reveals the concession permits expire in thirty days unless a feasibility survey is filed. If no engineer certifies the route, the claims lapse forever. Emotional beat: hope with a deadline attached.

chapters.title: Provisions and Old Wounds
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Preparing for the upstream trek, Mara and Eli argue over their father's death and Eli's choice of company over family. They set out anyway, bound by blood if not trust. Emotional beat: loyalty tested before the trail even begins.

chapters.title: The Gorge Crossing
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. A rope bridge over the Silverthread gorge collapses under their gear; Eli nearly drowns and Mara saves him. First proof the wilderness forgives nothing. Emotional beat: fear sharpened into resolve.

chapters.title: The Claim Jumpers
chapters.summary: Eli's POV. They encounter armed men staking false markers ahead of schedule — hired by Eli's own firm to secure the ground regardless of the survey. Eli says nothing to Mara. Emotional beat: complicity taking root.

chapters.title: Amos's Cabin
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. They shelter in Amos's abandoned cabin and find his journal: he was a company surveyor who refused to falsify the ore reports and was driven into the hills. Emotional beat: Mara sees her own future in his ruin.

chapters.title: River Rising
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Back in Kestrel Falls, spring melt floods the lower town while company agents pressure residents to sell. Ada organizes resistance and sends word upriver. Emotional beat: a town deciding what it is worth.

chapters.title: The Split Trail
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. At a fork, the safe route adds four days they don't have; the dangerous canyon route might make the deadline. Eli argues for caution — really buying time for the claim jumpers. Emotional beat: suspicion's first cold drop.

chapters.title: Canyon of Echoes
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The canyon passage nearly kills them in a rockslide; digging free, Mara finds fresh dynamite crates stamped with her old employer's mark. Emotional beat: betrayal confirmed, grief arriving before anger.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Source
chapters.summary: Mara and Eli's alternating POV. At the headwaters, Mara confronts Eli with the evidence. He confesses the firm planned to use her certification to legitimize the claim all along. Emotional beat: love against duty, both bleeding.

chapters.title: The Survey
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. With days left, Mara surveys the route honestly and finds what Amos found: the line is buildable only by damming and diverting the source. Her signature would be a death sentence for the valley. Emotional beat: expertise turned weapon against its owner.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: Eli's POV. Racing downstream to file or refuse the report, they're ambushed by the firm's enforcers who want the map and the journal destroyed. Eli takes a bullet shielding Mara. Emotional beat: sacrifice as apology.

chapters.title: Deadline Eve
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Mara reaches Kestrel Falls at dusk on the final day, carrying wounded Eli and the journal. The company's lawyer waits with filing papers and an offer: sign, and Eli's medical costs and her career are restored. Emotional beat: temptation priced exactly to her wounds.

chapters.title: The Refusal
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Before the assembled town, Mara publicly refuses to certify the route, reads Amos's journal aloud, and files instead a formal finding that the line is unbuildable without destroying the watershed. Emotional beat: truth spoken at personal ruin.

chapters.title: Enforcers at the Falls
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The firm attempts to seize the records by force; the town — miners, shopkeepers, the sheriff — stands them down at the depot until a territorial inspector arrives with expired permits in hand. Emotional beat: collective courage, ordinary people holding a line.

chapters.title: What Burns
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The claims lapse. Mara burns her old survey drafts on the riverbank — not in defeat but release — and sits with Eli as he begins his slow recovery, forgiveness unfinished but begun. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into peace.

chapters.title: The Keeper of Maps
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Weeks later, the town asks Mara to stay and chart the valley properly — not for rails or ore, but for the people who live there. She accepts, redrawing Amos's map with the source marked protected. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, not inherited.

chapters.title: Where the River Begins
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, coda. One year later, Mara leads Eli — walking again, working the town's new school — up to the headwaters at last light. The river runs clear. She leaves Amos's original map buried in a cairn where it was always headed. Emotional beat: homecoming, quiet and earned.
